text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm opening a refactor PR to split `modules/compute` into `compute-core` + `compute-network` and to tighten provider pins. Want a quick sanity check before I land the state moves.
raj: quick Q: will this require `terraform state mv` for existing instances or can we keep resources under the same module path? :thinking:
maya: We will need a handful of `state mv` ops for aws_instance resources because the module namespace will change. I added a migration script in the PR that does `terraform state mv` + plan validation.
oliver: ping the ops runbook — prefer doing the state mv in canary region first. Also what are the exact provider pins you want to apply?
maya: plan is to switch module `required_providers` to explicit exacts in the registry lockfile and set `required_providers` in root to `aws = { source = "hashicorp/aws", version = "4.54.0" }` and in modules use `>= 4.54, < 5.0` only as compatibility. Then regenerate the provider lockfile with `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64`.
kyle: CI currently fails when modules have unconstrained provider ranges. Our policy prefers exact lockfile entries, but allows ranges in module `required_providers` as long as lockfile is checked in. Does your PR include the regenerated `.terraform.lock.hcl`?
maya: yes — PR includes lockfile. I also added a `make regen-lock` target and a CI job that validates lockfile sha against the approved list. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2486
ci-bot: ci/lockfile-check — failed on a previous run (missing platform entry). Please run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64,linux_arm64` if you support both.
maya: good catch — will add linux_arm64. Another issue: our Helm chart mounts service creds via a hostPath symlink under `/etc/secrets/service-creds` which breaks when we change module volumes during the split. Planning to switch to a Kubernetes Secret and projected volume to avoid subPath symlink issues.
raj: can you paste the manifest snippet? The subPath bug was causing crashes in our canary last week.
maya: sure:
```
volumes:
  - name: service-creds
    hostPath:
      path: /etc/secrets/service-creds
containers:
  - name: app
    volumeMounts:
      - name: service-creds
        mountPath: /var/run/creds
        subPath: creds.json
```
Switch to:
```
volumes:
  - name: service-creds
    projected:
      sources:
        - secret:
            name: app-service-creds
            items:
              - key: creds.json
                path: creds.json
```
oliver: LGTM. That projected volume avoids symlink/subPath races during rolling restarts.
kyle: minor nit — update the helm values schema and add a migration note in `RELEASE_NOTES.md` so SREs know to recreate the k8s Secret if they still use hostPath in on-prem clusters.
maya: will do. Also tagging in the PR: @kyle @oliver for review. If we land this, can we do a staggered rollout: apply module split + lockfile in canary, run acceptance tests, then state mv for canary only, then roll to prod?
oliver: yes. Do the `state mv` last after we confirm resources behave under the new module path. And keep an automated rollback step to move state back if plan shows diffs.
raj: sounds good. I'll review the migration script. If folks are happy, I can coordinate the canary apply this afternoon. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks — I've added a check-list in the PR description and a small script `scripts/migrate_compute.sh` that performs prechecks and dry-run plan. Please comment on the PR for any additional edge cases.
terra-bot: reminder — when changing provider versions, run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64,linux_arm64` and commit `.terraform.lock.hcl` per infra policy.
maya: will run the full lock regen + push in the next push. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
